title: Гиперадренокортицизм
terminology: Clinically relevant hyperadrenocorticism requires a compatible progressive multisystem pattern, routine laboratory context and an interpretable selected endocrine test.
Isolated ALP, thin skin, breed, appearance, stress cortisol, incidental adrenal enlargement or one positive screen does not prove Cushing syndrome.
Significant nonadrenal illness, pain, hospitalization, stress and recent glucocorticoid exposure can reduce test interpretability and trigger a timing gate.
Every glucocorticoid route is inventoried, including oral, injectable, otic, ophthalmic, skin, inhaled and hidden products.
Clinically relevant hypercortisolism is confirmed before pituitary-versus-adrenal differentiation.
Endogenous ACTH and adrenal imaging support differentiation after confirmation; bilateral or discordant findings require specialist review.
Rare feline hyperadrenocorticism defaults to specialist-authored workup and commonly retains diabetes/fragile-skin context.
Iatrogenic phenotype and HPA-axis suppression risk remain separate from spontaneous disease, and abrupt withdrawal is unsafe.
Diabetes, infection, hypertension, thrombosis, pancreatitis and treatment-induced hypoadrenal states retain separate evidence and urgent routes.
Treatment monitoring integrates water, appetite, panting, skin, muscle, quality of life and protocol-specific safety rather than one cortisol value.
External timed tests, imaging and surgery return to the same patient and preserve protocol, sample and timing identity.
No drug, dose, taper, dynamic-test protocol, washout interval or surgical threshold is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Измерены ли вода и мочеиспускание одинаковым способом во времени?
Как менялись appetite, panting, abdomen, muscle и skin?
Какие oral, injected, ear, eye, skin, inhaled или hidden glucocorticoids использовались?
Есть ли acute illness, pain, hospitalization или major stress?
Есть ли diabetes, infection, pancreatitis или thrombosis signs?
Какой endocrine test, protocol, timing, sample и lab?
Imaging выполнено до или после подтверждения hypercortisolism?
Есть ли pacing, behavior change, seizure или vision change?
Как менялись BP, weight и muscle strength?
Какие infection sites, cytology/culture и recurrence задокументированы?
Как фактически выполняется текущий план и есть ли adverse/hypoadrenal signs?
Какие home-monitoring, cost и referral ограничения реальны?

variants.title: Клинически обоснованное подозрение или высокий риск ложноположительного теста
variants.diagnosticTruth: Endocrine screening is justified by a compatible progressive multisystem clinical and routine-laboratory pattern after all-route glucocorticoid inventory and nonadrenal-illness assessment; incidental findings and uninterpretable positive screens do not establish disease.

presentations.complaint: Progressive PU/PD, polyphagia, panting, abdominal enlargement, muscle loss and skin changes align with a compatible routine-lab pattern.

historyAnswers.all_route_glucocorticoid_inventory: All routes reviewed without explanatory exposure.
historyAnswers.acute_illness_pain_hospital_stress: No major interpretability blocker or blocker explicitly resolved.

examFindings.finding: Signs and routine findings combine; none acts alone.
Protocol and sample identity remain external evidence.

investigations.result: Compatible progressive pattern and exposure inventory.
Testing interpretable now or deliberately delayed.

followUp.timing: after routine workup, selected screen and confirmation review

outcomes.safe: A high-quality clinical suspicion proceeds to an interpretable selected test.
outcomes.unsafe: Appearance or one lab value directly becomes Cushing syndrome.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the pattern justifies testing but does not itself prove cortisol excess.

presentations.complaint: An adrenal nodule/enlargement or liver/ALP change is found incidentally without a convincing progressive Cushing pattern.

historyAnswers.measured_water_and_urination_trend: No objective compatible trend or uncertainty retained.

examFindings.finding: Function and anatomy remain separate questions.
Review/monitoring may be safer than forced screening.

investigations.result: Imaging alone cannot pass confirmation gate.

followUp.timing: clinical trend and incidental finding review without automatic endocrine treatment

outcomes.safe: Incidental anatomy is monitored or investigated on its own merits.
outcomes.unsafe: An adrenal nodule or isolated ALP value automatically diagnoses Cushing syndrome.

ownerCommunication: Explain that an adrenal finding may be nonfunctional and must not be confused with confirmed hormone disease.

presentations.complaint: Major nonadrenal illness, pain, hospitalization, stress or recent glucocorticoid exposure makes endocrine testing misleading or unsafe to interpret now.

historyAnswers.endocrine_test_protocol_timing_lab: Any prior test timing and limitation retained.

examFindings.finding: Stabilization and later review precede elective screening.
No fixed washout interval is invented.

investigations.result: Full exposure and concurrent disease context.

followUp.timing: after concurrent disease stabilization and reviewed exposure interval

outcomes.safe: The urgent disease is managed and endocrine uncertainty remains explicit.
outcomes.unsafe: A stressed sick patient is labeled confirmed from a random high result.

ownerCommunication: Explain why testing now could spend money while producing a misleading answer.

variants.title: Гипофизарно-зависимый гиперадренокортицизм
variants.diagnosticTruth: Pituitary-dependent disease requires confirmed clinically relevant hypercortisolism plus compatible differentiation; bilateral adrenal change is supportive rather than sufficient, neurologic macroadenoma concerns trigger pituitary imaging, and long-term control is judged clinically with safety monitoring.

presentations.complaint: Clinically relevant hypercortisolism is confirmed and post-confirmation evidence supports a pituitary-dependent pattern.

examFindings.finding: Endogenous ACTH and full context retained.

investigations.result: Compatible pituitary pattern or specialist-integrated evidence.

followUp.timing: post-differentiation baseline then clinical and safety checkpoints

outcomes.safe: PDH is assigned after confirmation and compatible differentiation.
outcomes.unsafe: Bilateral adrenal appearance or small breed decides the cause.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the cortisol syndrome was confirmed before evidence was used to locate its source.

presentations.complaint: A confirmed/supported pituitary-dependent patient develops pacing, altered behavior, vision change, seizures or other intracranial concern.

historyAnswers.acute_illness_pain_hospital_stress: Neurologic status cannot be inferred from endocrine control.

investigations.result: Pituitary size/brain context and competing lesion.

followUp.timing: urgent neurologic route then endocrine/neurologic trajectory

outcomes.safe: Neurologic progression receives targeted imaging without changing every stable PDH case.
outcomes.unsafe: New neurologic signs are dismissed as old Cushing behavior.

ownerCommunication: Explain why these new signs change the need for brain/pituitary imaging.

presentations.complaint: A treated pituitary-dependent patient needs longitudinal clinical, complication and hypoadrenal-safety monitoring.

historyAnswers.current_treatment_actual_use_and_adverse: Actual use and adverse signs reconciled.

examFindings.finding: Water, appetite, panting, skin, muscle and QoL integrated.
No blind dose increase is generated.

followUp.timing: reviewed protocol checkpoints plus continuous home trend

outcomes.safe: Control balances clinical benefit, safety and quality of life.
outcomes.unsafe: One cortisol result or persistent symptom causes automatic escalation.

ownerCommunication: Explain which home changes indicate benefit and which require urgent safety contact.

variants.title: Надпочечниково-зависимый гиперадренокортицизм
variants.diagnosticTruth: Adrenal-dependent disease requires confirmation of clinically relevant hypercortisolism before post-confirmation differentiation and staging; unilateral, bilateral, invasive or metastatic anatomy changes specialist options but does not by itself prove function or choose a side.

presentations.complaint: Clinically relevant hypercortisolism is confirmed before a unilateral adrenal mass is used for differentiation and staging.

followUp.timing: post-confirmation staging and specialist decision checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Function and staging precede an individualized specialist route.
outcomes.unsafe: An incidental unilateral mass automatically triggers diagnosis or surgery.

ownerCommunication: Explain separately what proves hormone excess and what imaging says about surgical feasibility.

presentations.complaint: Bilateral nodules, asymmetric glands or discordant endocrine/imaging evidence prevents a simple pituitary-versus-adrenal assignment.

historyAnswers.owner_monitoring_cost_and_referral_feasi: Advanced endocrine review feasible or referral needed.

examFindings.finding: No side or cause is selected randomly.

followUp.timing: specialist differentiation checkpoint before irreversible decision

outcomes.safe: Discordance stays visible until specialist integration.
outcomes.unsafe: The engine guesses a gland or cause from ambiguous anatomy.

ownerCommunication: Explain that bilateral findings can have several meanings and must not be resolved by guessing.

presentations.complaint: Confirmed adrenal-dependent disease has possible vascular invasion, metastasis or major comorbidity affecting surgery versus medical/palliative planning.

followUp.timing: staging handoff then route-specific safety and QoL monitoring

outcomes.safe: Risk and goals guide a specialist decision with uncertainty explicit.
outcomes.unsafe: Imaging alone declares curable, inoperable or mandates surgery.

ownerCommunication: Give a staged range for operability and complications without promising the final route.

variants.title: Ятрогенный гиперадренокортицизм и подавление HPA-оси
variants.diagnosticTruth: Iatrogenic hyperadrenocorticism and HPA-axis suppression require compatible phenotype plus complete glucocorticoid exposure across every route; abrupt withdrawal is unsafe, and any change, taper, stress support or emergency protocol remains clinician-reviewed.

presentations.complaint: A compatible Cushing phenotype follows prolonged systemic glucocorticoid exposure with possible HPA-axis suppression.

historyAnswers.all_route_glucocorticoid_inventory: Systemic product, timing and actual use fixed.
historyAnswers.current_treatment_actual_use_and_adverse: Current exposure and adverse signs reconciled.
historyAnswers.acute_illness_pain_hospital_stress: Current stress demand and illness recorded.

followUp.timing: reviewed exposure-change and clinical/hypoadrenal safety checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Iatrogenic disease and suppression risk are managed through a reviewed change plan.
outcomes.unsafe: Exposure is stopped abruptly or relabeled spontaneous without inventory.

ownerCommunication: Explain why the medicine may cause both Cushing signs and withdrawal risk.

presentations.complaint: Non-oral or hidden glucocorticoid exposure from ear, eye, skin, inhaled or repeated products explains a compatible phenotype or test distortion.

historyAnswers.all_route_glucocorticoid_inventory: Every route, household product and prescriber inventoried.
historyAnswers.current_treatment_actual_use_and_adverse: Actual frequency and overlap recorded without generating dose judgment.

followUp.timing: after coordinated reviewed exposure change and safety monitoring

outcomes.safe: Hidden routes are discovered and coordinated without an invented taper.
outcomes.unsafe: Only tablets count and testing proceeds as if exposure did not exist.

ownerCommunication: Ask for every bottle and device; explain that local products can still affect the hormone axis.

presentations.complaint: Withdrawal or intercurrent illness reveals weakness, anorexia, vomiting, collapse or shock compatible with adrenal suppression risk.

followUp.timing: continuous emergency handoff then reviewed axis and underlying-disease plan

outcomes.safe: Potential suppression is treated as an urgent safety problem with regimen details externalized.
outcomes.unsafe: Symptoms are dismissed or the engine invents a stress dose/taper.

ownerCommunication: State that sudden weakness after medication change can be urgent and needs immediate reviewed care.

variants.title: Осложнённый случай или мониторинг лечения
variants.diagnosticTruth: Diabetes/insulin resistance, hyperlipidemia, infection, hypertension, thrombosis, pancreatitis and treatment-induced hypoadrenal risk remain separate evidence-based complications; urgent states are treated first and the endocrine plan is reconciled rather than blindly increased.

presentations.complaint: Confirmed/suspected hypercortisolism coexists with diabetes, insulin resistance or hyperlipidemia, especially in a rare feline specialist case.

historyAnswers.diabetes_infection_pancreatitis_thrombos: Diabetic control, ketone/pancreatic signs and timing fixed.
historyAnswers.measured_water_and_urination_trend: PU/PD cannot be assigned to one disease without evidence.
historyAnswers.current_treatment_actual_use_and_adverse: Both plans and actual use reconciled.

examFindings.finding: Neither diagnosis is inferred solely from the other.

investigations.result: Diabetes, lipid and pancreatic complication status.

followUp.timing: acute diabetic/pancreatic stabilization then parallel endocrine monitoring

outcomes.safe: Both diseases remain measurable and acute metabolic risk is prioritized.
outcomes.unsafe: Poor diabetic control automatically proves Cushing or triggers blind endocrine escalation.

ownerCommunication: Explain which findings belong to diabetes, which support cortisol disease and why both must be followed.

presentations.complaint: Recurrent urinary, skin, ear or other infection is suspected during hypercortisolism or its treatment.

historyAnswers.infection_sites_culture_cytology_history: Site, dates, prior cytology/culture and response fixed.

investigations.result: Additional risk factors and routine context.

followUp.timing: site-specific infection response then endocrine/recurrence checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Infection is confirmed and followed without losing the endocrine context.
outcomes.unsafe: Cushing status alone diagnoses infection or justifies endless empirical treatment.

ownerCommunication: Explain that cortisol disease increases risk but testing the actual site is still necessary.

presentations.complaint: Acute dyspnea/collapse, limb or neurologic event, severe hypertension concern, abdominal pain/vomiting or hypoadrenal treatment signs require urgent complication routing.

historyAnswers.current_treatment_actual_use_and_adverse: Actual use, recent changes and adverse signs fixed.

examFindings.finding: Cause and treatment toxicity remain competing.

followUp.timing: continuous emergency handoff then complication/endocrine recovery

outcomes.safe: The acute complication is stabilized and the endocrine plan is reconciled with evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: Acute decline causes an automatic treatment increase or routine appointment.

ownerCommunication: State which red flags are time-critical and that the cause may be complication or treatment effect.

familyValidationRules: Reject if isolated lab sign, appearance, breed or incidental adrenal mass proves Cushing syndrome.
Reject if major nonadrenal illness or glucocorticoid exposure is ignored when interpreting a test.
Reject if differentiation or imaging occurs before clinically relevant hypercortisolism is confirmed.
Reject if non-oral glucocorticoid routes are omitted or abrupt withdrawal is called safe.
Reject if infection, diabetes, thrombosis, pancreatitis or hypoadrenal risk loses its separate evidence route.
Reject if code generates a drug, dose, taper, dynamic-test protocol, washout interval or surgical threshold.
